Read levels of a pyramid file

Source: R/read.R
a5_read_pyramid.Rd

Reads the rows of the tiles at lod whose bounding boxes meet bbox, as a renderer does for a view: the footer first, then only those tiles' row groups, or their data pages where row groups hold several tiles. Selection is by tile, so rows of a selected tile that lie outside bbox are returned too; filter the cells afterwards for an exact cut.

Usage

a5_read_pyramid(src, lod = NULL, bbox = NULL)

Arguments

src

Path of a pyramid Parquet file written by a5_write_pyramid().

lod

Integer vector of the LODs to read, each one of the file's (see a5_pyramid_info()), or NULL (default) for every level.

bbox

NULL (default) for everywhere, or c(xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax) in WGS 84 degrees. For a box across the antimeridian give xmin > xmax, such as c(179, -1, -179, 1).

Value

A tibble with the columns of a5_pyramid(), in file order: ascending LOD, then cell id; with an owner column (an a5R::a5_cell) and the weights column where the file has them. A file without lod or ncell columns gives its level and 1.

See also

a5_pyramid_info() for the file's levels and tiles.

Examples

library(a5R)
centre <- a5_lonlat_to_cell(-3.19, 55.95, resolution = 10)
cells <- a5_uncompact(a5_spherical_cap(centre, 3000), resolution = 15)
path <- tempfile(fileext = ".parquet")
a5_write_pyramid(data.frame(cell = cells, value = runif(length(cells))), path)

a5_read_pyramid(path, lod = 12)
#> # A tibble: 22 × 4
#>    cell               lod ncell value
#>    <a5_cell>        <int> <int> <dbl>
#>  1 6316007800000000    12    18 0.557
#>  2 63bb939800000000    12    16 0.569
#>  3 63bb93c800000000    12    16 0.575
#>  4 63bb940800000000    12    46 0.500
#>  5 63bb941800000000    12    62 0.507
#>  6 63bb942800000000    12    66 0.526
#>  7 63bb943800000000    12    66 0.505
#>  8 63bb944800000000    12    48 0.541
#>  9 63bb945800000000    12    66 0.499
#> 10 63bb946800000000    12    62 0.470
#> # ℹ 12 more rows
a5_read_pyramid(path, lod = 15, bbox = c(-3.2, 55.94, -3.18, 55.96))
#> # A tibble: 1,024 × 4
#>    cell               lod ncell  value

#>  2 63bb940060000000    15     1 0.366 
#>  3 63bb9400a0000000    15     1 0.170 
#>  4 63bb9400e0000000    15     1 0.512 
#>  5 63bb940120000000    15     1 0.680 
#>  6 63bb940160000000    15     1 0.628 
#>  7 63bb9401a0000000    15     1 0.932 
#>  8 63bb9401e0000000    15     1 0.0711
